`\x1b\](.*?)\x1b\\` matches OSC (Operating System Command) sequences.
`\x1b([(@-Z\\-_]|\[[0-?]*[ -/]*[@-~])` matches other escape sequences.
The second part `([(@-Z\\-_]|\[[0-?]*[ -/]*[@-~])` is a group.
`[@-Z\\-_]` matches a single character in the range `@` to `Z`, `\`, `-`, `_`.
`\[[0-?]*[ -/]*[@-~]` matches CSI (Control Sequence Introducer) sequences.

The issue says: "This commit updates the ANSI parser to ignore the `\x1b0`-`\x1b?` escape sequences".
`\x1b0` to `\x1b?` are characters with codes 48 to 63.
In ASCII:
0: 48
1: 49
...

The current regex for single-character escape sequences is `[@-Z\\-_]`.
